# Damage classes (beyond REPDF C1–C10)

## DMG-001 — Compound faults (proposed)

Two or more C-class faults in one file (e.g., C2+C9, C5+C10).

- Maps to: C2, C9, C5, C10
- Generator: Apply k in {2,3} generators from C1-C10/DMG in random order; seed recorded per file.
- Realism: Real damage (disk, transfer) is rarely single-component (CLM-0006).
- Evidence: CLM-0006, CLM-0023

## DMG-002 — Mid-file block holes (proposed)

One or more 512 B/4 KiB aligned blocks zeroed or replaced with foreign data (bad sectors, unallocated clusters).

- Maps to: —
- Generator: Zero or overwrite N aligned blocks at uniform offsets; N and block size parameterised.
- Realism: Storage-level loss is sector/cluster granular; carving motivation (CLM-0023).
- Evidence: CLM-0023

## DMG-003 — Head truncation / missing prefix (proposed)

The first K bytes missing (carved from mid-file, partial recovery).

- Maps to: C1
- Generator: Drop the first K% (5-50%) of bytes.
- Realism: Carved and recovered fragments often lack the header region.
- Evidence: CLM-0023

## DMG-004 — Object-stream corruption (proposed)

Damage inside a compressed /ObjStm, losing many objects at once.

- Maps to: C5, C9
- Generator: Flip/zero bytes within one ObjStm's compressed data or its /First offset table.
- Realism: PDF >=1.5 packs most objects in ObjStm; REPDF's C2 only removes a classic xref table.
- Evidence: CLM-0023

## DMG-005 — Cross-reference stream damage (proposed)

Damage to a /Type /XRef stream (not a classic table).

- Maps to: C2, C3
- Generator: Truncate/flip bytes in the xref stream or its /W /Index fields.
- Realism: Modern producers emit xref streams; untested by REPDF.
- Evidence: CLM-0023

## DMG-006 — Fragmented / interleaved file (proposed)

File carved as out-of-order or interleaved fragments with foreign data between.

- Maps to: —
- Generator: Split into F fragments, shuffle, interleave with foreign bytes; ground-truth order kept.
- Realism: Carving from disk/RAM yields fragmented data (REPDF motivation, untested).
- Evidence: CLM-0023

## DMG-007 — Distributed bit rot (proposed)

Random bit flips across many streams (aging media, transmission).

- Maps to: C9
- Generator: Flip B random bits over the file with density parameter.
- Realism: Aging media and transmission errors cause scattered or bursty bit errors across many streams. Note that REPDF's C9 already substitutes 12-30 bytes over 11-28 streams (OBS-0002); this class adds realistic error models (burst length, sector alignment, density) rather than more of the same.
- Evidence: CLM-0004, OBS-0002

## DMG-008 — Broken incremental update (proposed)

A truncated or corrupted incremental-update section on top of an intact base revision.

- Maps to: C3, C10
- Generator: Append an update, then truncate/corrupt within it.
- Realism: Incrementally-updated (edited/signed) PDFs are common; prior revisions are recoverable evidence.
- Evidence: CLM-0023
